dossiers.name: OnKure Therapeutics
dossiers.what: Designs small-molecule cancer drugs targeting PI3K-alpha, one of the most commonly mutated cancer drivers, aiming to hit the mutant protein while sparing the normal version — which is what causes the severe blood-sugar side effects limiting existing PI3K drugs. After deprioritizing its first-generation candidate it is rebuilding around two next-generation molecules. No revenue.

bull: The market is paying less than nothing for the pipeline: $176.4M cash against a $166M market cap gives an enterprise value of NEGATIVE $7.8M, with essentially no debt and a 26.8x current ratio.
Financing risk is off the table for ~3 years — an oversubscribed $150M private placement closed end of Q1 2026, and cash is guided into 2029, well past the 1H 2027 IND filings.

Multi-year data vacuum: INDs not until 1H 2027 means first-in-human data realistically lands in 2028. Cash covers it; nothing else does. A $19.50 target rests on preclinical molecules.

Clean Energy revenue grew 43% and Pipeline runs an 18.4% EBITDA margin — broad-based, not one hot segment.

Structural tailwinds it is directly levered to: grid modernization and electrification (Power Delivery), the data-center power build-out (the $1.65B Superior Group deal adds a data-center electrical platform), utility-scale renewables, and fiber/5G. These are multi-year spend cycles, and MasTec is a scale contractor of choice.

Profitable and de-levering with a Strong Buy consensus: ~$16B TTM revenue, ~$495M TTM net income, net debt only ~1.5x guided EBITDA, 0.88 beta. Twenty analysts average a $422 target vs $241 today — and the stock trades in the lower quarter of its 52-week range ($171–$441) after a ~45% pullback from the high.
bear: Contractor economics are lumpy and low-margin: consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin is only ~8.8%, projects carry execution, weather and change-order risk, and free cash flow was NEGATIVE in H1'26 (-$47.6M) on working-capital build — cash generation is back-half-weighted and can slip.

Cyclical and policy-exposed: Clean Energy depends on the renewables/IRA incentive environment, Pipeline on oil & gas capex sentiment, and all segments on customer capital budgets that can be cut in a downturn or higher-for-longer rate world. The 52-week chart already shows a >40% peak-to-trough drawdown.

Acquisitive growth adds integration and balance-sheet risk: the $1.65B Superior Group deal (closed 2026) inflates reported growth and must be integrated; net debt sits at $2.4B, and a single large troubled project can swing a quarter given the thin margins.
